## Code of Conduct

This project and everyone participating in it is governed by our
[Code of Conduct](CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md). By participating, you are expected
to uphold this code. Please report unacceptable behavior to
[forums.lanik.us](https://forums.lanik.us).

## How Can I Contribute?

### Reporting Bugs

Before creating a bug report, please check existing issues to avoid
duplicates. When you create a bug report, include as many details as
possible:

- **Use a clear and descriptive title** for the issue
- **Describe the exact steps to reproduce the problem**
- **Describe the behavior you observed** and what you expected to see
- **Include relevant logs, error messages, or screenshots**
- **Specify your environment** (OS, shell version, etc.)

### Suggesting Enhancements

Enhancement suggestions are welcome! When suggesting an enhancement:

- **Use a clear and descriptive title** for the issue
- **Provide a detailed description** of the proposed enhancement
- **Explain why this enhancement would be useful** to most users
- **Include examples** of how the feature would work

### Your First Code Contribution

Not sure where to start? Look for issues labeled:

- `good first issue` - Simple issues suitable for beginners
- `help wanted` - Issues where we need community assistance

## Pull Request Process

1. **Fork the repository** and create your branch from `main`:

   ```bash
   git checkout -b feature/your-feature-name
   ```

2. **Make your changes** and ensure they follow our style guidelines.

3. **Test your changes** thoroughly before submitting.

4. **Update documentation** if needed:
   - Update the README.md with details of changes to the interface
   - Include new environment variables, exposed ports, useful file
     locations, and container parameters

5. **Follow semantic versioning** ([SemVer](https://semver.org/)) when
   updating version numbers in example files and README.md.

6. **Ensure any install or build dependencies** are removed before the
   end of the layer when doing a build.

7. **Submit your Pull Request** with a clear title and description
   explaining:
   - What changes you made
   - Why you made them
   - Any relevant issue numbers (use `Fixes #123` or `Closes #123`)

8. **Wait for review** - You may merge the Pull Request once you have
   the sign-off of two other developers. If you do not have permission
   to do that, you may request the second reviewer to merge it for you.

## Style Guidelines

### Commit Messages

- Use the present tense ("Add feature" not "Added feature")
- Use the imperative mood ("Move cursor to..." not "Moves cursor to...")
- Limit the first line to 72 characters or less
- Reference issues and pull requests liberally after the first line

### Code Style

- Follow existing code conventions in the repository
- Comment your code where necessary
- Write clear, self-documenting code when possible
- Include appropriate error handling

## Getting Help

If you need help or have questions:

- Open a [GitHub Discussion](../../discussions) or issue
- Visit [forums.lanik.us](https://forums.lanik.us) for community support
